cards.b: Music that tells a story or paints a picture.
Single-movement orchestral work based on a story, poem or scene; Vltava is one.
'My Homeland': Smetana's cycle of six symphonic poems; Vltava is the second.
Using a country's folk tunes, dances or stories to express national identity.
Flexible tempo: speeding up and slowing down expressively.
Harmony using many notes from outside the key; richer and more tense.
Larger than Classical: more brass, piccolo, harp, more percussion.
A short recurring theme linked to a character, object or idea.
A short pattern repeated many times.
Very rapid repetition of a note, e.g. on strings, to create tension.
Two or more different rhythms played at the same time.
Ballet from 1913 famous for driving rhythm, irregular metre and dissonance.
Main recurring melody; minor at first, later in major; changes instrument and dynamic.
Orchestral piece before a drama; a concert overture stands alone, e.g. Mendelssohn.

short.q: Give three features of Romantic music.
short.model: Expressive lyrical melody, chromatic harmony, large orchestra, wide dynamics and tempo changes, programme music, nationalism.
It depicts a Czech river and uses a folk-style polka for the wedding scene, expressing the national identity of Bohemia.

short.q: How does Smetana use the river theme to hold the piece together?
short.model: It returns many times, changed in key (minor to major), orchestration and dynamic, so there is unity and variety.

short.q: Describe how film composers use the orchestra to build tension.
short.model: Tremolo strings, dissonant chords or clusters, ostinato, a gradual crescendo and rising sequences, low brass and percussion.

short.q: Compare a Romantic and a Classical orchestra.
short.model: The Romantic orchestra is larger with more brass, percussion, piccolo and harp, giving a bigger sound and more colours.
